title: Akshita Sood Introduction Video(Hitwicket)
transcript:
Hi everyone, I'm Akshata Sood, a fourth year computer science student at VIT Bhopal University, specializing in cloud computing and automation with a CGPA of 8.97.

If I had to describe myself in few words, I would say that I'm curious, love building things, and genuinely enjoy solving problems that I haven't encountered before.

During college, I have explored areas like DSA, full stack development, AI and GenAI. I have built projects like Novex scoring agent, which uses AI to generate full stack web applications from natural language prompts, and Advira, an AI powered rag chatbot.

What I enjoy most is taking an idea, experimenting with different technologies, and turning it into something real. This mindset has also helped me solve 300+ coding problems, achieving a 3-star CodeChef rating, and taking up leadership responsibilities at VIT through technical events, CTFs, hackathons, and workshops.

Beyond technology, I am also someone who really loves animals and cares deeply about helping people and animals who are in need. I hope that as I grow in my career, I can use my skills, my opportunities, and my resources to create a positive impact beyond just technology.

Coming to gaming, what fascinates me is that you are not just building a software, you are building an experience. Games combine technology, strategy, competition, user experience, psychology, and constant experimentation. And that's what attracted me to Hitwicket.

I love how it takes something as familiar and loved as cricket and turn it into a strategic gaming experience where players make decisions, build teams, compete, and constantly improve. I am excited about this opportunity because I want to learn quickly, take ownership, experiment, and see the impact of what I build.

I believe my background in software development, cloud computing, and AI can bring a unique perspective to a gaming product.

For me, getting to work at the intersection of technology, gaming, and cricket would be a really exciting opportunity. Thank you for watching.
summary: Akshata Sood, a fourth-year computer science student specializing in cloud computing and automation, introduces her academic background, technical skills, and projects. She highlights her experience in full-stack development, AI, and competitive programming, alongside her leadership roles in university events. Finally, she expresses her strong interest in joining Hitwicket, explaining how her background in software development and AI can contribute to their strategic gaming products.
keyPoints: Akshata Sood is a fourth-year computer science student at VIT Bhopal University with an 8.97 CGPA, specializing in cloud computing and automation.
Her technical portfolio includes full-stack development, AI, and GenAI, featuring projects like the Novex scoring agent and the Advira RAG chatbot.
She has solved over 300 coding problems, earned a 3-star CodeChef rating, and led technical events, CTFs, and workshops at her university.
She expresses a strong passion for gaming, specifically highlighting Hitwicket's strategic cricket gameplay as an exciting opportunity to apply her skills.

title: AkshitaSood Video
transcript: Hi, I am Akshata Sood, currently pursuing my BTech in Computer Science and Engineering at VIT Bhopal University. I really enjoy solving coding problems and building projects because they help me learn something new every day. If I look back at the past year, I think my biggest improvement I've made is that I became much more disciplined, confident, and open to learning new projects. Earlier, I was only interested in frontend development. I loved designing and interfaces and building websites, but after some time, I realized that I wanted to understand how an entire application works, not just the not just what the users see. So, I started learning backend development on my own. In the beginning, it really felt very difficult and challenging, because there were so many things, so many concepts like APIs, databases, authentication, server-side development, and much more. But, instead of getting discouraged, I kept building projects, reading documentation, and learning from my mistakes. Recently, I've also started exploring tools like Docker because I want to understand how applications are deployed in real-world environments. Along with improving technically, I also worked on myself as a person. I became more disciplined by following a daily routine and staying consistent with my learning. I also realized that communication is just as important as the technical skills are. Earlier, I was very underconfident while explaining my ideas, but then I started working on it. I started speaking more during presentations. I used to discuss with my friends, used to tell them how what what my projects are all about, their working, and, yeah, I practiced whenever I got the chance. Over time, I became much more comfortable in expressing myself. So, this whole journey taught me that growth doesn't happen overnight. It's the small, small things which you do every day which, you know, just make the biggest difference. I still have to learn a lot of things, but today, if I look back at my past year, yeah, so, I'm much more confident, disciplined, and excited to keep improving myself. Thank you so much.
summary: Akshata Sood, a BTech Computer Science and Engineering student at VIT Bhopal University, shares her journey of technical and personal growth over the past year. She discusses transitioning from frontend development to learning backend technologies and Docker, while also improving her discipline, confidence, and communication skills.
keyPoints: Akshata is pursuing a BTech in Computer Science and Engineering at VIT Bhopal University.
She expanded her skills from frontend development to backend development, learning concepts like APIs, databases, authentication, and server-side development.
She recently began exploring Docker to understand how applications are deployed in real-world environments.
She focused on personal growth by establishing a daily routine for discipline and practicing communication through presentations and project discussions.
